lines.trans: Mr. Muranishi! May we ask you a few questions?
Why did you come here? Please stay away from her from now on!
Even if you show up this late, there is nothing you can do!

words.gloss: now after all this time, too late

lines.trans: Do you have any idea how much she was looking forward to filming a new work with you back then?

words.gloss: something to look forward to; fun

lines.trans: Do you understand how deeply she trusted you all this time? You trampled over every bit of it!
And it wasn't only you. I keep wondering whether I was making her suffer this whole time too.
Holy Mary, Mother of God, for us sinners...
Pray for us now and at the hour of our death. Amen.
Mr. Muranishi, what caused her suicide attempt? Did your breakup have something to do with it?

meanings.note: Attached to surnames, given names, or company names to show everyday respect; never used for oneself.
Covers everything from a casual chat to a business deal or idea.

examples.trans: Let us have a little talk.

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.

examples.text: 皆様、あちらのほうでお伺いいたしますのでどうぞ。
examples.trans: Everyone, I will take your questions over there, so please come this way.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.
Read なん before だ/です/の, and なに before が/を or alone.

examples.text: 何を買いにきましたか。
examples.trans: What did you come to buy?

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Irregular verb: くる -> きます -> きました.
In もういい, means 'already enough' or 'ready now'.
Attached to names of children, close friends, or familiar acquaintances.

examples.text: トシちゃん、また来たの？
これで金輪際、俺たちには関わらないでください！
examples.trans: With this, swear you will never have anything to do with us again!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Follows a verb's て-form or polite お + stem (お待ちください, お持ち帰りください) to make a polite request.

examples.text: ここに書いてください。

できる.gloss: be built; open; be able to

meanings.en: come into existence; be completed; can do
meanings.note: With buildings or stores (店ができる), means a new shop has been built or opened.

examples.text: 駅前に新しいカフェができました。
examples.trans: A new café opened in front of the station.

examples.text: 日本語が少しできます。
examples.trans: I can speak a little Japanese.

meanings.note: Polite/dialectal negative ending, especially in ～ません.
Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Filler or polite attention-getter.

examples.text: あの、ちょっとよろしいですか。
examples.trans: Excuse me, do you have a moment?

examples.text: あの、実は相談があります。
examples.trans: Um, actually I have something to ask you.

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: Limits the preceding noun or phrase to that item alone.

examples.text: これだけお願いします。

meanings.note: Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).

meanings.en: know; find out; be aware of
meanings.note: Godan verb; state of knowing is 知っている.

examples.text: 彼の電話番号を知っていますか。
examples.trans: Do you know his phone number?

examples.text: 本当の理由を知りたい。
examples.trans: I want to know the real reason.

meanings.note: Standalone pronoun ('this'), unlike この which requires a noun.

meanings.en: nothing more than (after past verb); up to
meanings.note: After a plain verb + です (出店したまでです), modestly states 'we simply did that and nothing more'.

examples.text: 念のため聞いたまでです。
examples.trans: I merely asked just in case.

meanings.note: Ichidan verb; potential form 信じられる means 'can believe' (信じられない = unbelievable).

examples.text: あなたの言葉を信じます。
そんなこと、信じられません。
examples.trans: I can't believe such a thing.

meanings.note: 分かってる asks or states ongoing understanding; plain past 分かった means 'got it! / I understand'.

examples.text: 日本語が少し分かります。

examples.trans: Got it, I will come right away.

meanings.note: In casual speech, それ plus は often fuses into そりゃ ('well, as for that / of course').
With で (全部で), means 'in total' or 'altogether'.

examples.text: これまでどれだけ信じてたか分かってますか？それ全部踏みにじったんですよ。
